title_fb: Why tonight may beat GTA 6 launch day
hook: This will surprise you. Tonight may be the best part of G T A 6.
open_loop: Lines 1-2 withhold why tonight could be the best part; the study (lines 4-6) pays it off: people were happier before their trip than after.
payoff: Vacationers were happier before the trip, and after it the extra happiness was gone (Nawijn et al. 2010). Honest limit: a vacation study, not a game study. Enjoy the wait.

lines.visual: SCENE 1 (frame 0): Benny in psych outfit, shocked face, pose shock, headline 'SURPRISE' already on screen; snap-zoom on 'surprise'.

lines.text: Tonight may be the best part of G T A 6.
lines.say: Tonight may be the best part of G, T, A, six.
lines.visual: SCENE 2 (on 'Tonight'): Benny smug, headline 'TONIGHT' with a plain moon-colour dark-blue background. SCENE 3 (on 'best'): stamp 'BEST PART' slams (thud), Benny gasps. On 'G': badge 'GTA 6' plain text pops.

lines.text: Benny waits all night outside the store.
lines.visual: SCENE 4: Benny in a sleeping-bag pose (slump to hop), cheering and yawning in turns, generic plain store door at right with no logo or sign; badge 'ALL NIGHT' on 'all night'. GAG: he nods off, jerks awake, hops with joy.

lines.text: A study tracked the happiness of 1,530 adults.
lines.say: A study tracked the happiness of one thousand, five hundred thirty adults.
lines.visual: SCENE 5: Benny thinking, brain prop; on 'one thousand' a counter climbs to 1,530 (suffix ' ADULTS' only after it lands, ding). No other text.

lines.text: Before their trips, vacationers were happier than others.
lines.visual: SCENE 6: two bars with labels only, no numbers: 'VACATIONERS' tall, 'OTHERS' short; Benny happy, flex. Headline 'BEFORE' on 'Before'.

lines.text: After the trip, the extra happiness was gone.
lines.visual: SCENE 7 (on 'After'): the tall bar sinks to equal height with the other (buzz, shake), Benny slumps, expression broke. On 'gone': stamp 'GONE' slams (thud).

lines.text: That was a study about vacations, not games.
lines.visual: SCENE 8: Benny shrug, honest face, headline 'VACATIONS' on 'vacations', then 'NOT GAMES' on 'not' (max 2 words each).

lines.text: Enjoy tonight. Which do you pick? Comment A or B.
lines.visual: SCENE 9 (on 'Enjoy'): Benny happy in the sleeping bag. SCENE 10 (on 'Which'): rows 'A: THE WAIT', 'B: THE GAME' pop; Benny points at viewer on 'Comment'. Rows only, no footer.
lines.on_screen: A: THE WAIT / B: THE GAME

facts_used.claim: Nawijn et al. 2010: 1,530 Dutch adults tracked; vacationers were happier than non-vacationers before their trip (anticipation is the suggested reason); after the trip overall no difference; a very relaxing break gave a small boost that wore off by eight weeks.
Same study, bibliographic summary (Applied Research in Quality of Life 5(1), 35-47).

math_check: No arithmetic beyond the sample size: 1,530 adults (974 took a vacation, not used in the script). Voice 'one thousand, five hundred thirty', caption/screen 1,530. Word count computed by script.

upload.title: Why tonight may beat GTA 6 launch day #Shorts
upload.description:
The happiest part of a big wait may be the wait itself.
Would you pick the wait or the game? Comment A or B.
A study of 1,530 adults found vacationers were happier before their trip, and the extra happiness was gone after it. It studied vacations, not games.
Source: Nawijn et al. 2010, Applied Research in Quality of Life.
